title: Why Use JSON Schema from DuckDB?
description: Validate JSON columns against a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) contract directly in SQL — no Pydantic / ajv / jsonschema-Python in a sidecar. Best fit: ingest-time data-quality gates, ETL contract checks, and one-query enrichment that fills in declared `default` values. Built on the [pboettch/json-schema-validator](https://github.com/pboettch/json-schema-validator) C++ library; the validator's primary target is [JSON Schema draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes).

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: JSON Schema is the de facto contract language for JSON payloads. This extension makes those contracts executable from inside DuckDB so you don't need a separate Python or Node.js step to enforce them.

bulletPoints.label: Ingest-time data quality
bulletPoints.description: Filter rows that don't satisfy the schema before they reach a clean table — `json_schema_validate` returns `BOOLEAN`, so it drops straight into a `WHERE` clause.

bulletPoints.label: Lint your contracts
bulletPoints.description: Run `json_schema_validate_schema` against the schema itself before deploying. Catches typos in the schema before they cause every row to fail validation.

bulletPoints.label: Default-value enrichment
bulletPoints.description: Use `json_schema_patch` to compute the [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) operations that bring an incomplete document into conformance with the schema's declared `default` values, or `json_schema_update` to apply them inline.

bulletPoints.label: Audits and dashboards
bulletPoints.description: Aggregate `valid` / `invalid` counts over a column of JSON in one query — much simpler than pulling rows out to a Python validator and back.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Internally, this is a thin DuckDB scalar-function wrapper around [pboettch/json-schema-validator](https://github.com/pboettch/json-schema-validator) and [nlohmann/json](https://github.com/nlohmann/json). Both schema and data are passed as DuckDB `JSON` values. There's no `ATTACH`, no secret type, no network — pure local validation against an in-query schema string.

bulletPoints.label: Four scalar functions
bulletPoints.description: `json_schema_validate` and `json_schema_validate_schema` return `BOOLEAN`; `json_schema_patch` and `json_schema_update` return `JSON`. All four take their schema and data inline — no preregistration step.

bulletPoints.label: Draft compatibility
bulletPoints.description: Primary target is [JSON Schema draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes). The `$schema` keyword in your document is honored where the underlying validator supports it; for newer drafts ([2019-09](https://json-schema.org/specification-links#2019-09) / [2020-12](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema)), test the keywords you actually use rather than assuming full coverage.

bulletPoints.label: Schema features in scope
bulletPoints.description: Type validation (`string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`), `required`, `properties`, numeric `minimum` / `maximum` / `multipleOf`, string `minLength` / `maxLength` / `pattern` / `format`, array `minItems` / `maxItems` / `uniqueItems`, and the `default` keyword used by `json_schema_patch` / `json_schema_update`.

bulletPoints.label: Pairs with DuckDB JSON
bulletPoints.description: Combine with [DuckDB's JSON support](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/overview) — `read_json_auto`, `JSON` type, [`json_extract_*`](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/json/loading_json.html) — so the validator slots into the existing JSON pipeline rather than replacing it.

sections.title: What to know before relying on it
sections.description: Honest scoping for production use. The extension is small and focused; it doesn't try to be every JSON-Schema validator out there.

bulletPoints.label: Boolean validation, not error reports
bulletPoints.description: `json_schema_validate` returns `TRUE` / `FALSE`. It does not return a structured list of which keywords or paths failed — for that level of diagnostic detail, validate at the application layer with [ajv](https://ajv.js.org/) / [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/json_schema/) / [jsonschema](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/) and use this extension as a coarse SQL gate.

bulletPoints.label: No `$ref` resolution across files
bulletPoints.description: Schemas are passed as a single `JSON` value per call — there is no filesystem or HTTP `$ref` resolver. Inline any `$ref` targets into the same schema document before validating.

bulletPoints.label: Not a replacement for typed columns
bulletPoints.description: If your data has a fixed shape, modeling it with proper DuckDB columns plus [`CHECK` constraints](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/constraints) is cheaper and clearer. JSON Schema validation is for the genuinely-JSON case where the shape is contract-defined but the storage stays opaque.

bulletPoints.label: Performance scales with schema complexity
bulletPoints.description: Deeply-nested schemas with many keywords run the full validator per row. For very large tables, validate on ingest into a staging table rather than re-running the check on every read.

useCases.title: Quality gate on ingest
useCases.description: `INSERT INTO events_clean SELECT * FROM events_raw WHERE json_schema_validate(:schema, payload)` — non-conforming rows can be tee'd into a quarantine table for manual review.

useCases.title: Audit a JSON column
useCases.description: Aggregate `valid` and `invalid` counts with `json_schema_validate` inside `COUNT(*) FILTER (...)`. Useful for retroactively checking historical data against a freshly-tightened contract.

useCases.title: Fill in missing defaults
useCases.description: Declare `default` in the schema, then use `json_schema_update` to produce the enriched JSON in one expression — or `json_schema_patch` when you need the diff for an audit log.

useCases.title: Lint schemas before deploying
useCases.description: `json_schema_validate_schema` over a table of candidate schemas in CI. Catches typos before they reject every production row.
